note: Window agent m1000-m0901, 2 Nov 2026. One event, two keyframe overrides, two rulings. Judah: its founding region 'Judea' reaches north into the Samaria hills, and its keyframe then dropped those cells, leaving the heart of Israel unowned. Twenty-first and Twenty-second Dynasties: their -1000 and -943 keyframes drew Cliopatria's whole Egypt outline (Western Desert, Red Sea, Matruh: +759 cells at each seam) although the pages name only the Delta and capitals; both now match the ledger (Delta, plus the priests' Nile valley for the Twenty-second) and the neighbour window's -1077 correction. Kush: a ruling gives it the 42 cells south of the first cataract that the Theban priests took by the size rule (the succession rule then carries them to Kush for the Twenty-second Dynasty). Bit Adini: the 60 and 90 km Carchemish discs swallowed Til Barsip, which the page puts south of Carchemish.

region.text: the Samaria hills (the gazetteer's Samaria) where the gazetteer's Judea reaches beyond Judah's frontier (the -900 shape), outside the contested Benjamin border band: Israel's land round Shechem and Samaria

events.note: c. 930: the founding event's region 'Judea' (Hebron to the Samaria hills, 32.46 N) takes Israeli cells that Judah's own keyframe then drops, leaving six cells round Shechem and Samaria owned by nobody. The page draws Judah's frontier narrowly: 'The northern border of Judah extended east-west from the northwestern shore of the Dead Sea, passing near Jericho to the area of Gezer'; Benjamin joined Judah, with Geba and Mizpah 'on his side of the border' and Ramah 'on the border, less than ten miles from Jerusalem'. Shechem, where the Israelites gathered, and Samaria are in the north. The cells beyond that frontier, outside the contested Benjamin band the next event of the ledger draws, go back to Israel. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: region intersected with the gazetteer's Samaria; without it the spec (22 cells) also took in the Philistine coast and Judah's south below Hebron, and the loss handed Israel 5 southern Judah cells that Israel's -930 keyframe dropped again the same year.]

correction.text: Lower Egypt, the Delta around Tanis, the land the pharaohs 'controlled'; Middle and Upper Egypt are the High Priests' land and reach the map through the ledger's vassal relation (the same shape as m1100-m1001 keyframe_overrides/2 gives -1077..-1001)

keyframe_overrides.why: The keyframe drew Cliopatria's whole Egypt outline, which adds 759 cells (New Valley 525, Red Sea 180, Matruh 48) to the ledger's Delta and snaps the state at -1000. The page: 'The pharaohs of the Twenty-first Dynasty ruled from Tanis, but were mostly active only in Lower Egypt, which they controlled'; 'the High Priests of Amun at Thebes effectively ruled Middle and Upper Egypt in all but name'. It says nothing of the Western Desert, the Red Sea hills or the Libyan frontier. Same correction as the neighbour window's -1077 keyframe (m1100-m1001 keyframe_overrides/2); the priests' land comes through the ledger's vassal relation; valid -1000..-944, the dynasty ending in 943.

union.text: the Delta around Bubastis and Tanis
the Nile valley of Middle and Upper Egypt, the Theban priests' land

correction.text: the Delta around Bubastis and Tanis plus the Nile valley of Middle and Upper Egypt and the Fayyum, the land the ledger gives the dynasty (the priests' former land, assumed from 943); not Cliopatria's whole outline

keyframe_overrides.why: The keyframe drew the whole Egypt outline of Cliopatria's last New Kingdom shape, 'unverified for the south', which adds 759 cells (New Valley 525, Red Sea 180, Matruh 48) beyond the ledger's Delta plus the former priests' Nile valley (assumed by the dossier; the 21st Dynasty page has the priests ruling 'Middle and Upper Egypt in all but name') and snaps the state at -943. The page names no land beyond the capitals: 'its rulers almost certainly governed from Tanis, which was their capital' (Manetho: 'first ruled over Bubastis'). Held to -901 so the correction stays in this window; the -900 keyframe of the next window re-draws the outline from -900.

region.text: the land south of Carchemish (the city's latitude, 36.83 N, the dossier's coordinate), in the bend of the Euphrates, without the city's own cell

rulings.why: The 60 km Carchemish disc (and the 90 km one before -975) lies over Bit Adini's disc and the size rule gave the capital's land to Carchemish from -975, leaving Bit Adini a crescent. The page: Bit Adini is 'usually thought to have been in the bend of the Euphrates River, south of Carchemish', 'with its capital at Til Barsip (now Tell Ahmar)'. South of Carchemish's latitude the land goes to Bit Adini, north of it the size rule stands. The line is an approximation: the page gives no frontier. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: the city's own cell (centre 36.77 N) lay inside the polygon and went to Bit Adini from -1000 to the end of the window; carved out with a 10 km disc. North of the line the size rule gave Bit Adini (the smaller claim) Carchemish itself in -1000..-976; rulings/2 gives those cells to Carchemish.]

The Nile Valley region of the Theban priests (and of the Twenty-second Dynasty after them) runs down the whole Aswan governorate to the Sudan border, so 42 cells south of the first cataract, inside Kush's -1000 shape (bbox from 23.8 N), went to the Egyptian side by the size rule and cut a strip of Egypt through Lower Nubia. The page: Kush 'referred to the region south of the first cataract in general', 'the first cataract at Elephantine usually being considered the traditional border between the two polities'; 'With the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC ... Kush became an independent kingdom centered at Napata'; Kashta, in the 8th century BC, was the one who 'extended Kushite control north to Elephantine and Thebes'. The page gives no early border of its own (silent on c. 1000-900), so the traditional border at the cataract stands: the contested cells south of it are Kush's.

region.text: Carchemish and its 60 km district (the dossier's own disc from -975) north of the city's latitude, with the city's own cell

rulings.why: Companion to rulings/0 (added by the reviewer, 2 Nov 2026): Carchemish itself and its district north of the city's latitude stay Carchemish's. Bit Adini's 70 km disc is smaller than Carchemish's 90 km disc of -1175..-976, so the size rule gave Bit Adini the city of Carchemish for 25 years; the page puts Bit Adini 'in the bend of the Euphrates River, south of Carchemish', 'one of the two chief states of the Aramean-held territories in the Euphrates along with Carchemish'. The outer ring east of the Euphrates (between it and the Balikh, where the page also puts Bit Adini) is left to the size rule. From -975 Carchemish's 60 km disc is the smaller claim and the size rule already decides the same way.
